sections.What this is: The ice surface of every year 2016 to 2026, on the day of the satellite picture the site shows for that year (2016 09-29, 2017 10-04, 2018 09-24, 2019 09-29, 2020 08-19, 2021 09-23, 2022 09-18, 2023 10-13, 2024 08-23, 2025 10-07, 2026 09-27). It is a physical model fitted to every dated elevation model that exists for the glacier, not an interpolation between two surveys. Where a flight or the lidar was flown, the surface of that day is reproduced (to about 0.2 m, the DSM epoch weighted by its own noise); between and beyond the epochs the surface follows the surface mass balance, the melt timing and a fitted rate of ice flow. A model, not a measurement, except on the days and cells a survey covers.
sections.Observations:
• Flights (swisstopo Spezialbefliegungen, photogrammetric DSM 0.5 m, each tied to rock with a plane, 0.7 m): 4 flights over the ice on 2018-09-11, 2019-09-03, 2021-08-14, 2022-07-15; 16 further flights (2017-08-22, 2018-09-11, 2019-09-03, 2019-09-04, 2020-08-07, 2020-09-14, 2021-08-14, 2022-07-15, 2023-08-10, 2023-08-21, 2024-08-20, 2025-09-19) reach the strip only over rock: they cover less than 1 % of the ice and are no observation of it.
  • Lidar (swissSURFACE3D raster, one day per tile from the point clouds, 0.35 m): 26 tiles flown 2021-08-24 to 2021-09-22.
  • swissALTI3D 2019 edition and the newest edition as ice surfaces (stereo; the model takes their uncertainty as 0.6 m below 2000 m and 1.5 m above, 2.0 m above 2000 m where no flight series exists). Their dates were estimated from the flights (the date at which the edition equals the flight-based surface of the tongue): 2019 edition 2015-09-21, newest edition 2023-09-06.

Against the flight and lidar based surface the editions stand too high at the upper end of the flight coverage: A1 2019 edition: +0.3 m at 3650 m, +0.5 m at 3750 m, +0.6 m at 4050 m; A2 newest edition: -0.6 m at 2750 m, -0.6 m at 2950 m, -1.0 m at 3050 m, -1.3 m at 3150 m, -1.7 m at 3250 m, -1.5 m at 3350 m, -0.9 m at 3450 m, -1.1 m at 3550 m, -0.6 m at 3650 m, +0.5 m at 3850 m, +1.7 m at 4050 m. This was measured and removed; above the reach of the flights it is held constant (+0.5 m added to the editions' uncertainty there).
sections.Physics and fitted numbers:
h(x,t) = h0(x) + S(z,t) + e(x)·τ + residual

  • S is the surface mass balance acting on the surface: the GLAMOS elevation-band balance of Corbassière as a stand-in (GLAMOS has no balance for this glacier; computed, and said so here).
    • Winter accumulation is spread over October to April.
    • Summer melt is spread over May to September in proportion to the positive degrees of the Eggishorn (2892 m) and Jungfraujoch temperature records (lapse rate 0.65 K per 100 m).
    • Snow melts first (density 0.4), then ice (0.9) or firn (0.6).
  • e(x) is everything the balance does not explain, mainly ice flow, fitted per cell. Median by elevation, in m/yr:

Ice area and volume are computed inside the 3D strip (bed: Grab et al. 2021 ice thickness; ice where the surface stands more than 0.5 m above it); the strip holds only part of the glacier, so these are not the GLAMOS whole-glacier figures.
sections.Validation:
ICESat-2 (not used in the fit): model minus 680 shots on the ice, median +1.33 m, NMAD 1.25 m, rmse 2.21 m. 2019: +1.22 m (275 shots). 2021: +0.23 m (43 shots). 2025: +1.59 m (362 shots).

Leave one flight out (refit without it, predict it): rmse 1.9, 1.8, 2.5, 2.4, 2.5 m (flights in date order; the rmse contains the 8 m crevasse detail of the DSM).

Fit residual on all 870,060 observations: NMAD 1.07 m, rmse 1.60 m.
sections.Uncertainty: 1σ, honest ranges: on a flight or lidar day on the cells it covers 0.3 to 0.7 m; between flights 1.8 to 2.4 m (leave one out); beyond the last flight about 2.5 m; where only the editions exist (above the reach of the flights) about 2.2 m (ICESat-2 rmse) with an absolute offset of up to 2 to 3 m; the first year before any observation about 3 m; the last year (balances estimated) about 3.6 m. ICESat-2 reads about 0.9 m lower than surface models on rough ice (not a model error).
sections.Not done, and remarks:
• Ice flux. The rate of ice flow e(x) was fitted from the surfaces; it has not been checked against the ice flux (flux divergence from ITS_LIVE velocities and the thickness map). Left open on purpose.
  • High accumulation area. Where neither lidar nor flights exist the surface rests on the two swissALTI3D editions (stereo, stated accuracy 1 to 3 m), on the mass balance and on a constant rate of ice flow. The change from year to year is better known there than the absolute height (about 2 to 3 m).
  • Ice edge. At the margin the ice surface is continued up the wall for at most 32 m (flat, only over rising ground); the Swiss Glacier Inventory 2016 supports it only weakly.
  • Terms. The terms of use and the accuracy statement of the flight DSMs have not been read.
